ateret-zekenim/1:_: One may not knead, etc. The lamed in shelanu should be pointed with kamatz and not patach, for otherwise it speaks of him alone like u-lanu in Gibeah (so too in his Shulchan Aruch). If one kneaded, it is forbidden only in eating but in benefit it is permitted immediately before it comes to leavening; even where it is impossible, one should not permit even b'dieved since there is concern for leavening — unlike what Shulchan Aruch wrote to be lenient in a time of pressure. However, water drawn while it was still day and left overnight, or after the beginning of the night and left overnight, is permitted even l'chatchila.
baer-heitev/1:א: Close to bein hashemashot. By right one should draw them at bein hashemashot itself; and since not everyone knows how to measure bein hashemashot, therefore one draws them close to bein hashemashot after sunset (before moonrise). B'dieved, if one drew them while it was still day or drew after the beginning of the night, it appears from the words of the later authorities that one may be lenient to knead with them after 12 hours; and in responsum of Magen Avraham siman 32 he wrote one should not be lenient unless in a time of pressure or great loss. See Taz who wrote it is better after drawing than to draw early. However Maharil wrote the opposite — end quote: it is better to draw a little early than to delay — see Ateret Zekenim; his words appear correct and so implies Magen Avraham. Kaf HaChayim.
baer-heitev/1:ד: On the night of the 5th. Explanation: for those who bake at Motzei Shabbos and cannot draw at Motzei Shabbos nor on Friday evening when they need to draw at bein hashemashot and Shabbos does not prepare for Yom Tov (and if not for preparation it would certainly be permitted, for all shevut is permitted at bein hashemashot) — therefore they draw on the night of the 5th that belongs to the 6th day, Beit Yosef; if so, also those who bake on the second day of Yom Tov are forbidden to draw at bein hashemashot on Yom Tov, for one Yom Tov does not prepare for another and they need to draw on the eve of the 14th. It appears to me that if he forgot to draw on the night of the 5th he may draw on Friday while it is still day on this Erev Pesach. Or he may command a gentile to draw at bein hashemashot — see siman 307. Or he may take water drawn in his house even though not drawn for the sake of the mitzvah, since it is impossible otherwise. Magen Avraham; see Kaf HaChayim.
baer-heitev/1:ז: Designated. One should say at the time of drawing for the sake of matzah of the mitzvah — Maharil and Mahariv; and Maharil wrote further that some are accustomed to take designated water each night independently.
baer-heitev/2:ב: Pressure. If he has drawn mayim shelanu in his house he should take them even though there is concern they were drawn by day or at night — Kaf HaChayim, Ateret Zekenim. And in Halakhot Ketanot part 1 siman 97 he is lenient regarding rainwater collected from the air at night.
baer-heitev/3:ב: Lukewarm. That is, like the warmth of saliva; and it is explained in Tur and Beit Yosef that in benefit it is permitted for everyone even if one kneaded with hot water.
baer-heitev/4:_: One in two. It implies specifically one in two, Beit Yosef; but Semag and Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote it is nullified in the majority, and so too in Yoreh De'ah siman 98, Magen Avraham; and it is implied from the words of the poskim that if it became mixed during kneading it is not nullified — we require specifically that it became mixed before kneading. (And Kaf HaChayim ruled in the name of his brother-in-law the Gaon, may he rest in Eden, that he permitted even at the time of kneading.) And Ateret Zekenim raised that b'dieved one may permit even in such a case. And Magen Avraham wrote it appears permitted to mix them l'chatchila, for the reason is not because of prohibition but when not left overnight they are hot and when mixed they become cold; if so, it is permitted to cool them l'chatchila — requires study. And Kaf HaChayim wrote the same applies to copper-kettle water — this cooling helps according to all — and so too Ateret Zekenim.
baer-heitev/5:א: Salt. But after baking it is certainly permitted to scrape the faces of the matzot with salt water and return them to the oven as they do on Chol HaMoed. And specifically on Chol HaMoed it is permitted to scrape, but on the first two nights it is forbidden — see Taz.
baer-heitev/5:ב: To forbid. That is, in eating; but in benefit it is certainly permitted. And if he put a little salt in it, if it is baked immediately it is permitted in eating, for a little salt does not heat it entirely — Magen Avraham. And all this if one kneaded with water; but if one kneaded with fruit juice, Bach ruled one should not forbid b'dieved.
baer-heitev/6:ב: Matzah. And in Rambam it implies it is rich matzah. And for everyone one must eat a kezayit of matzah aside from spices. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/6:ג: And pepper. Even one grain makes the entire dough chametz; and the same applies to a little lime — Darkei Moshe. It appears specifically when kneaded into it; but if it fell on it one removes it and it is permitted. It appears ginger is treated like pepper, and possibly the same for anise and saffron. Magen Avraham and Ateret Zekenim ruled to permit in eating all kinds of spices except pepper. And even in pepper one forbids only in eating like salt, as written in s.k. 15; and so Bach, Ateret Zekenim, and Kaf HaChayim. Dough kneaded in wine into which beer became mixed — Hagahot Beit Yosef wrote that since there is no water there is no need to be particular — Ateret Zekenim; see responsum Darkei Noam Orach Chayim siman 6 and Ginat Veradim general rule 4 siman 9.
beer-hagolah/3:ד: Tur in the name of Mahariv and Maharitz Gaon — according to his explanation they disagree regarding water that was not left overnight; and likewise Rambam in chapter 5
beer-hagolah/3:ה: Tur according to Rashi's explanation, and likewise the Rosh there
beer-hagolah/6:א: Rambam chapter 5, Rosh, and Mordechai end of chapter 3 of Pesachim — from that which is in Menachot 23
beur-hagra/1:א: (1) One may not knead. Rashi wrote the reason: because in the rainy season the sun travels in the lower parts of the sky and the springs boil, as written 94b. And R' Eliyahu Mizrachi wrote the reason: because at night the sun travels below the ground — see there; and their words appear from our words that by day springs are cold and at night they boil. And Rif explained what is written at the end of chapter Kol Sha'ah: the drawn water that was drawn on that day — and it is implied from his words that drawing from the attached source heats them and requires overnight standing; therefore he calls them drawn water because drawing heats them — see R' Eliyahu Mizrachi. According to Rashi, whatever stood 12 hours detached, even from morning until evening, is sufficient; and according to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi, specifically when it was not attached at night; and according to his words, even after the beginning of the night it is permitted to knead with them provided it was not attached at the beginning of the night. But R' Yehuda bar Natan wrote, and likewise Semak in the name of R' Yitzchak and Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 5, that the end of the night causes cooling because the north wind blows from midnight onward until dawn, as written at the beginning of Berachot; and it is cold, as written in Bava Batra 25b: from adulterers comes this north wind; therefore one must leave them the entire night — and so Rashba that one must leave them the entire night.
beur-hagra/1:ב: Between, etc. For Rashi, specifically cistern and spring water; but in rivers there is no concern, for specifically springs boil, as written in the Gemara: springs boil — and the reason is they are close to their exit from the source; and likewise according to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's explanation. And Rashi wrote: nevertheless one should not breach the fence of the early authorities; but according to Rif's explanation it is forbidden by law.
beur-hagra/1:ג: While it is still day, etc. For R' Eliyahu Mizrachi wrote that according to R' Eliezer of Metz one must draw them specifically at bein hashemashot so they remain attached all day, for by day springs are cold as written — and so Semak; and some are stringent to draw between day and night; and some forbid when drawn while it is still day even if left overnight afterward. Semak there rejected this because he mentioned only overnight standing — implying one need not be concerned when they were drawn, only that they stood overnight; and Beit Yosef rejected R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's words and explained "while it is still day or bein hashemashot" means only that one should not draw after the beginning of the night; but Beit Yosef was concerned for the stringent view and wrote close to bein hashemashot and not while it is still day. However, from the conclusion of all poskim and from the language of the Gemara it is implied like Shulchan Aruch's view; and likewise from Rif's language that he wrote they were drawn on that day.
beur-hagra/1:ד: And one may not knead, etc. To be concerned for R' Yehuda bar Natan's view as above.
beur-hagra/1:ו: And if the weather. To cool them specifically according to Rif's explanation, that the reason they became warm when drawn and need cooling.
beur-hagra/1:ח: And even. As written end of chapter 3 of Yoma: a cloudy day is entirely sun — for Rava's exposition: a woman should not knead, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ט: And if not. As Rambam and Shulchan Aruch siman 259 seif 8 wrote — see what is written there.
beur-hagra/1:כ: When it falls. For Shabbos does not prepare for Yom Tov, as written at the beginning of Yom Tov; and he follows his reasoning that he ruled one must draw them specifically at bein hashemashot or close to it — see Magen Avraham.
beur-hagra/1:פ: And it is customary to take. As written in Maggid Mishneh regarding Chanukah — and specifically in earthenware; see siman 453 seif 3.
beur-hagra/2:א: Seif 2: some say water. See Magen Avraham.
beur-hagra/3:א: Seif 3: one may not knead. Pesachim 42a — and they are equal that there is no, etc.
beur-hagra/3:ד: Whether with water. According to Rif's explanation, drawn water means water not left overnight, and the question also refers to water not left overnight.
beur-hagra/3:ו: And some say that b'shogeg, etc. For one transgressed intentionally as written chapter 2 of Yoma 17: they asked — if one transgressed and baked, etc.; and there it deals with intentional as written 99b, etc.; provided he does not deceive, etc.; this case of deception is different, etc.; 99b: one who cooks, etc.; and the first reasoning holds we also find one transgressed b'shogeg, as written chapter 3 of Shabbos: they asked — if one transgressed and stayed, what? And according to Rif's explanation there they asked regarding metsamek ve-yafeh whether it is forbidden b'shogeg — see Tosafot there; and proof from the pastries of Eretz Yisrael; and we are not concerned for such a case; but Rashi and Rosh rejected there and said because it is close to intentional; and all the more so for those who baked in our presence — see R' Eliyahu Mizrachi siman 226.
beur-hagra/4:_: Seif 4: water not, etc. And some say one in two, rather in majority as Semag and Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote; and the reason: since the majority is cold it cools — as Tosafot wrote Shabbos 42a s.v. noten; rather it appears as Rabbenu Tam says, etc.
beur-hagra/5:_: Seif 5: it is customary, etc. And even. They bring proof to forbid from what is written chapter 8 of Shabbos and in Gittin: matzah that is not salted; and in Chullin they said salted is like boiling and is like kneading in hot water — as above seif 3; and chapter 4 of Shabbos; and not regarding salt that adds vapor; and chapter 2 of Bava Batra: they distance salt because of heat — as written there in the Gemara. And this is what Baer Heitev wrote: and even b'dieved, etc.; and so Mordechai; and as above seif 3. But many poskim permit and reject their proofs: that which "not salted" means it lacks preparation like "not sharpened"; and that which "salted is like boiling" — they say there explicitly only when it is not eaten because of its salt — see Yoreh De'ah siman 98 and siman 105; and likewise that of Shabbos and Bava Batra where there is much salt; and Rashba siman 224 that it is not like boiling but to absorb and extract, etc.; but to heat, etc. And Ran brings proof to permit from end of chapter Kol Sha'ah from what is written: and soaked in water and salt is forbidden — implying specifically when cooking it heats; but for bread, no — and so Rashba, except he wrote people are accustomed to be stringent.
beur-hagra/6:א: Seif 6: since it has. In the Gemara there they say specifically that he added flour to it; and Tosafot wrote this sugya argues on that of Zevachim where they said even though the majority is rice, etc. — majority of Torah law; and we rule like the sugya of Zevachim that taste in a kezayit in a place of Torah law obligates, as Tosafot wrote; and likewise Tur explained in Yoreh De'ah; and this is what Shulchan Aruch wrote: since, etc.
beur-hagra/6:ב: Nevertheless. That Raavad in chapter 12 of Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot forbids in cooked dishes that leaven; and what is written in Menachot: seasoned, etc.; and in Tosefta and Yerushalmi chapter Kol Sha'ah: one fulfills with seasoned matzah — it deals with seasoning after baking; but in Yerushalmi chapter 2 halachah 4 it is not so, for they said there R' Simon in the name of R' Yehoshua ben Levi: that kezayit with which a person fulfills on Pesach must not have liquid enter it, etc.; and it was taught: one fulfills with seasoned matzah even though it has no taste of grain — they thought "seasoned" means liquids; it was stated: seasoned with sesame, seasoned with nuts — thus permitted even before baking, for after baking rich matzah does not apply; and as we wrote siman 462 seif 4; and so Raavad in Hilchot Matzah chapter 6 forbids because of rich matzah.
beur-hagra/6:ג: And pepper. For it is not called spice as Tosafot wrote chapter 1 of Yoma in the name of Tosefta; and pepper is likewise as spice — see Tosafot Pesachim 105a s.v. atei, etc.; and it heats as written in Niddah: she ate pepper and saw — see there in Shulchan Aruch siman 129.
beur-hagra/6:ד: And likewise. As written chapter 3 of Shabbos and chapter 2 of Bava Batra.
